sourceSufficiencyAssessment: Full text is preferred, not a universal gate. Actual primary essay/excerpt, owned selected Choice chapters and bounded procedural sources support this selected connected corpus. Goal/It's Not Luck are premise/role only and Handbook is authorship/contents only; candidate disclosures preserve those limits. The one retained-link omission has an available exact primary passage, so a local correction is sufficient.
mechanismAssessment: The capacity example preserves the direction 20 → 10 and the local/global distinction; bottleneck is not equated with mere low utilization. All five focusing steps and inertia are retained. Throughput is used in the supported sales/system-performance sense, not asserted as gross machine output or a new accounting formula. Policy is correctly rendered as rules, never political policy. DBR and project buffers are described at their bounded retained granularity; the conflict/assumption search and Choice ending are Goldratt/Efrat's arguments, not new management morals.
substantiveParityAssessment: All paired titles/bodies plus method and nine source notes read. Names, capacities, approximate 30% shortage estimate, conditional interventions, author/practitioner attribution and no-observed-results boundary survive both languages. No material translation inversion found.

findings.exactRu: Голдратт возвращается к нему после другой перемены: магазины могли бы часто заказывать проданное и держать меньше запаса, если BigBrand обеспечит быстрое пополнение.
findings.exactEn: Goldratt revisits it after another change: with rapid replenishment from BigBrand, stores could reorder what sold frequently and hold less stock.
findings.defect: The preceding screen explicitly explains large orders by their price advantage. The next screen removes that behaviour using rapid delivery alone, omitting the author's simultaneous change to the pricing basis. The unresolved incentive is part of the retained causal link, rather than an omitted unrelated technical chapter.
findings.minimalCorrectionRu: Голдратт возвращается к нему после двух перемен: быстрого пополнения и цены, зависящей от общего объёма продаж продукции BigBrand в магазине, а не от размера отдельного заказа. Тогда магазины могли бы ежедневно заказывать проданное и держать меньше запаса.
findings.minimalCorrectionEn: Goldratt revisits it after two changes: rapid replenishment and pricing based on total BigBrand sales in a store rather than the size of each order. Stores could then reorder each day what they had sold and hold less stock.
